### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`, touching **7** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/security/_activation/webhook (route, a path literal in reportUnownedRows; a path literal in runDeclaredWebhooks))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **39** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e2c976000d4c5184968fc6b189a965b59f21911e` — the merge of head `9eefd98b899ad3563fe5a10c31063df1cb3ebba4` into base `199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e2c976000d4c5184968fc6b189a965b59f21911e && git checkout e2c976000d4c5184968fc6b189a965b59f21911e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb 9eefd98b899ad3563fe5a10c31063df1cb3ebba4 && git checkout -B drift-repro 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb && git merge --no-ff 9eefd98b899ad3563fe5a10c31063df1cb3ebba4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `399e5501075e21e7f43cf9e794aa6c88a2d5b29b`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

- **S1 (webhookSlotSwitch) holds.** Only a package-less row while the environment declares nothing of the name is read as a name-keyed switch; a departed package's row answers no slot in either direction, at any holder count. A holder's own row still wins. `departedWebhookRows` excludes `null` and sorts. Matches ADR-0150 D8 (a row is its holder's switch, never another's).
- **should-fix S1 — ceremony: environment + package holders of one name.** In `runDeclaredWebhooks`, a customized copy naming no package under `holders.length > 1` writes `package_id = null`. When one of those holders is the environment (`null` in `declaredWebhooks.list()`), that row is not the name-keyed switch the note describes: `webhookSlotSwitch` returns it as the environment slot's OWN row (`rows.get(null)`), and the package holder ignores it (`!slots.includes(null)`). So the step silently picks the environment, and the note's sentence "switched off it keeps each holder with no row of its own off, switched on it turns none on" is false for that composition. Red line: ambiguity is reported, never guessed. Fix: for holders including `null` (and ≥2), either write no row and report naming every holder, or say truthfully that the row binds the environment's slot; add a pin for `[null, pkg]` in both list orders.
- **should-fix S2 — declaration.** The off-direction rows move persisted state's effect on upgrade with no operator action: "one holder, departed row off, holder shipped on: FROM holder off TO holder on" means outbound deliveries start for a webhook an operator had switched off. That is a public behaviour move on outbound HTTP, so `Clause-②` is `yes` (mixed: the departed-off cases widen delivery, the departed-on case narrows it), not `no`. Re-declare in the PR body and changeset, and add one operator line to the changeset: to keep such a webhook off, switch the holder off at `POST /api/v1/security/_activation/webhook/NAME?package=PACKAGE` (the warn already names the address).
- nit N1: `reportUnownedRows` returns after the departed-row warning, so under ≥2 slots a package-less row on the same name is never reported (once-per-name set). Fold both into one message or accept; no behaviour effect.
- `setActivation` matching by `(metadata_type, name)` regardless of `package_id`: pre-existing, noted in the PR, not in scope.

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks` and `@objectstack/cli` is acceptable for a D8 fix of a read the ADR already rules on; no export in the published index moves (`departedWebhookRows` is module-internal). `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. `Clause-②` → `yes` per S2.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author login `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); implemented by area E2 session_016WV4cyrFFk86Jqf7Mp5Rzw.
- Outbound side effect (webhook delivery) on upgrade, see S2.
- CI at this head: in progress when read (15:16Z), nothing red yet. No governed path, no `packages/spec/src/**`.

Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

S1 (code + pin) and S2 (declaration) → delta review by review#3 on the new head. N1 optional.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9eefd98b899ad3563fe5a10c31063df1cb3ebba4`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/declared-webhooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/declared-webhooks.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.generation-1.test.ts + none

Delta review of `399e5501..9eefd98b` by the reviewer of record 6879546273. With a narrowing arm now declared, this record is at the narrowing face over the whole non-prose diff (the webhook switch read at 399e5501 is unchanged apart from N1).

### ① Derived judgments

- S1 fixed: `ambiguous = unnamed && holders.includes(null)`. When the environment is a holder, a copy naming no package writes no activation row on either path (switch-only re-source and clone), and the note reports the copy's on/off and names every holder plus the per-holder address (no package for the environment). Two or more package holders without the environment keep the name-keyed package-less row, which `webhookSlotSwitch` reads as described. Pins for `[null, pkg]` in both list orders; ablation reported red without the fix.
- Accepted consequence, stated in the notes: in the ambiguous case a switched-off copy's state is not carried to any holder, so each holder follows its own row or declared default until the operator switches it. That is reporting, not guessing (red line), and the note gives the copy's state and the address.
- S2 fixed: `Clause-②: yes (widening; narrowing on a departed row switched on)` in the body and changeset, with an operator line that names the upgrade effect (deliveries resume) and the `?package=` address.
- N1 fixed: `reportUnownedRows` no longer returns after the departed warning; both kinds said once per name in one call (pinned).
- The S1 switch semantics reviewed at 399e5501 hold unchanged.

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks` and `@objectstack/cli`; the arm is now correct and complete. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. No published export moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Outbound side effect on upgrade (webhook deliveries resume for departed-off rows), now declared with an operator action.
- Author login `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); area E2 session_016WV4cyrFFk86Jqf7Mp5Rzw.
- CI at this head when read: 8 green, 18 running, none red. ACCEPT re-reads every check.

### ④ Design judgment

ADR-0150 D8 makes an activation row its holder's switch, never another's; reading a departed package's row as nobody's switch is the direct application, and the ceremony now refuses to pick a holder in the one composition where a package-less row would silently mean the environment. The outbound-delivery consequence is real but is the ADR's intended answer, and the release note plus warn give the operator the one action needed. Holds against the cited code and the card's scenario.

Implemented-by: `claude/area-E2-32695`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6`

**VERDICT: PASS**
